# Instagram adapter evidence

The adapter is original Airlock code. Implementation used the frozen contract and functional behavior inventory in the parent `planning/instagram.md`. No IGPlus JavaScript, CSS, selector rules, graphics, translations, or other assets were inspected or imported by the implementation worker. Earlier planning inspection is known, so this is **not a formal clean-room claim**.

On 2026-09-30, unauthenticated HTTPS requests to `https://www.instagram.com/` and `https://www.instagram.com/explore/` returned HTTP 200. Home contained no `a[href]`, `input`, `main`, `nav`, role, or accessible-label elements in the returned bootstrap HTML. Explore returned title `Popular on Instagram`, `<main role="main">`, status elements labelled `Loading...`, ordinary Home/login/signup/footer links, and a footer link to `https://www.threads.com/`. There were no images, videos, authenticated Search, inbox, Notes, profile, comments, or metric samples. This narrow observation supports the logged-out Explore-title classifier and a Threads footer-domain link classifier; it does not establish authenticated selectors.

A Playwright attempt using the installed Google Chrome executable in a separate temporary profile failed at launch under the sandbox with SIGABRT. The build worker then successfully checked public pages with bundled Chromium 153.0.8010.12 in an isolated profile at 1280 and 390 CSS pixels: Explore returned HTTP 200, title `Popular on Instagram`, one main region and zero Search surfaces; Following returned HTTP 200, title `Instagram`, zero main/Search surfaces, and login/signup UI. This confirms only logged-out Explore recognition; it cannot establish Following or authenticated Search behavior. No account was used, no credentials/content were captured, and no Computer Use was used. Raw public-response HTML was kept only temporarily outside the repository and is not an extension asset.

`instagram-semantic.html` and inline test fragments are original **synthetic semantic examples**, not sanitized live captures. Their test IDs are never production selectors. Link matchers use parsed same-origin URLs. Other matchers use standard HTML/ARIA and a small original English/Spanish concept vocabulary, with conservative post/inbox/navigation scope. No generated classes, graphic paths, positional layout rules, invented site-specific attributes, or assumed opaque identifiers are used.

Adapter enforcement is limited to the application host allowlist `instagram.com`, `www.instagram.com`, and `m.instagram.com`. The shared catalog's domain-family classification does not authorize application routing on auxiliary hosts such as `help.instagram.com`, `about.instagram.com`, or `i.instagram.com`; those receive no adapter matches or redirects.

## Experimental and unverified behavior

All authenticated DOM recognition is experimental pending representative live samples. Passing these tests proves scoped behavior and preservation on the stated semantic inputs, not compatibility with Instagram's current authenticated page experiments.

- Reels and Story/highlight URL decisions are tested, including direct singular Reel links, but browser/account behavior is not live verified. Profile/story controls that expose no semantic route/name may remain visible.
- Explore redirects only an identified discovery-only root. Search routes (`/search/`, `/explore/search/`, `/explore/tags/`, `/explore/locations/`) and root Explore with a Search surface remain available. Empty/bootstrap/unknown Explore layouts deliberately remain unredirected; unnamed authenticated discovery grids may remain visible. Width alone does not decide whether a surface is Search.
- `/?variant=following` is the inferred canonical Following destination from the functional specification; its current server/app behavior is unverified. Messages landing uses `/direct/inbox/` and affects Home only. No claim is made that Following removes all recommendation modules.
- Home posts require article semantics. Comments, Notes, story buttons/trays, and numerical cues require their corresponding accessible semantics. English/Spanish synthetic names have preservation tests; current localized site labels are unverified.
- Metrics hide identified numeric child elements while retaining profile navigation labels/actions. Counts embedded in a single unlabelled text node remain visible; arbitrary numeric captions/timestamps/messages are preserved.
- Badge changes require an identified unread cue in navigation. Conversation unread text remains available. This does not disable notifications.
- Threads link suppression requires navigation/header/footer scope; ordinary captions and shared DM links remain available. Promotions without identified navigation semantics may remain visible.
- Broad media covers HTML videos and images/avatars/attachments; runtime suppresses matched video playback. Account/auth/security routes and protected forms/dialogs are exempt. Images that provide the sole accessible name of a link/button remain available. CSS background images are deliberately not hidden because the shared whole-element effect would also remove their text/actions. CSS posters/controls not independently identified, unknown challenge markup, and live playback/restoration remain unverified. Media hiding is not network blocking.
- Fixtures exercise mutation-scope collection, preserved Search/DM composer/actions, profile links, post captions, and account/security media. Chrome/Firefox extension lifecycle, wide/narrow authenticated layouts, live locales, and real-site infinite scroll still need integration/live verification.
